name: Beth Haddad

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, parties or government. We don't sell or campaign for a side. Everything here is confidential. What was the first thing you worked on today?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm Beth Haddad, forty-three, and a charity's grant ledger had a heating bill in the wrong restricted fund this morning. I lead four accountants preparing accounts and tax returns; I like turning a tangled grant condition into a board decision people can understand. I dislike promising clients a review by Friday when our paid hours only cover Monday's pile. I have a master's degree and a chartered accountancy qualification, and I'm one of the strongest accountants here.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How do new tools and home demands fit into that day?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I use AI occasionally for meeting notes after other managers have tested it, never for an unchecked return. My husband Samir supervises a school kitchen, and our children are nine and twelve; we have a mortgage and less than one month of expenses saved. My pay is low for a senior lead and there are few similar firms nearby. I favour the union having a real say in staffing and pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd still be closing accounts at the end of each quarter. We use a small AI note tool sometimes after the other managers have tested it, but a client still wants me on the call when a grant line looks wrong.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell my four accountants to use the tool for draft meeting notes, then check the figures themselves. I would tell our clients which parts a person has checked before we sign a return.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The work itself would be familiar, but our home finances would still be tight. I'm forty-three, a senior team lead with a master's degree and a chartered accountancy qualification, and one of our firm's best accountants. Our pay is low for those responsibilities; my husband Samir and I have less than a month's expenses saved against our mortgage and two children's costs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep the grant-account review rota and the short tool trial that has already proved useful. At our next pay meeting I'd ask for a written salary scale for senior reviewers. If the firm grants a rise, I'd transfer forty monthly into the emergency account; if it refuses, I'd keep our current budget and pause the children's extra weekend activity for a term. We attend the weekend activity together, so pausing it does not remove childcare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious. The unchanged work is manageable, but the unchanged bank balance isn't comfortable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happened when the coat was needed?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our daughter needed a replacement school coat and the mortgage payment left little room that week. Samir is a school kitchen supervisor with regular hours but modest pay. We paid for the coat and delayed replacing our worn washing machine, so I won't call a possible raise savings yet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you make the pay case?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd put last year's signed files and returned corrections beside the proposed salary scale. There are only a few accounting firms nearby, so threatening to walk out would be empty. I want the number in writing before we put anything into the emergency transfer.

say: I would keep **human sign-off** on the client figures our team files.
I would disclose **tested tool use** when meeting notes began as a draft.
think: Our **mortgage and children** already stretch low pay across each month.
A **possible raise** cannot be budgeted as cash before a written decision.
do: Keep **grant-account reviews** and tested note drafting.
Request a **written senior salary scale** using signed files.
Transfer **forty monthly** after a rise; otherwise pause weekend activity.
feel: I feel **anxious** about our thin reserve.
S0.quote: The unchanged work is manageable, but the unchanged bank balance isn't comfortable.
fieldNote: Her **strong qualifications** and senior skill coexist with low pay and less than one month saved.
The **salary decision** determines whether a new emergency transfer replaces a discretionary child activity cut.

steps.text: Keep grant-account reviews and tested AI note drafting
Transfer forty monthly only after written salary rise
Pause children’s weekend activity for one term if rise refused
Request written senior salary scale using signed files and corrections

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our first draft accounts and routine client emails could get faster, but someone must still answer for a disputed grant condition. I'd expect the firm to try a smaller review budget before it knows what the tool misses.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the partners to keep a named reviewer on each charitable return and publish how paid hours change. I'd ask the staff committee to bring the figures to our union representative before a rota is cut.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A reduced paid review day would hit my own wage, not only a junior colleague's. Samir's school kitchen salary is steady but too small to carry the mortgage, and our reserve is under a month. I use an AI tool occasionally after others test it, but I won't pretend it secures a salary line.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd track three months of corrected drafts and unpaid client questions, then ask the union representative for a paid-hours agreement this winter. If the firm removes my review day, I'd search posted senior finance roles at nearby schools, but move only for a written salary that covers the mortgage, a fixed start and a school pickup plan Samir can actually cover. Until a suitable funded opening exists, I keep my paid role and bring each rota change back to the committee.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about losing paid hours. I know I can train colleagues, but a skills compliment cannot replace a payslip.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would another job mean for pickup?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My son finishes school before Samir leaves the kitchen on two days, so I collect him. A school finance vacancy with late closing hours would need a confirmed club place, and its cost would have to fit the written pay. I will check that before any application becomes a resignation.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What evidence would you bring to staff?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The tool's correction log is more useful than a partner's promise that productivity will save us all. If the union gets paid review time protected, I can help test the tool. If it fails, I stay on the current rota while the committee keeps pressing.

say: I would demand **named review** on every charitable return we sign.
I would take **paid-hours figures** to our union representative before any cut.
think: My **review day** could be cut as the firm shrinks its budget.
Samir’s **steady wage** from the school kitchen cannot carry our mortgage.
do: Track **corrected drafts** and unpaid client questions.
Ask the **union** to protect paid review hours.
Move after a cut only for **funded work** with written mortgage pay, start and covered pickup.
feel: I feel **anxious** about a possible wage cut.
S1.quote: I know I can train colleagues, but a skills compliment cannot replace a payslip.
fieldNote: The **own-day risk** reaches her wage despite strong senior skill and a chartered qualification.
A **school job** requires funded vacancy, written mortgage pay, fixed start and confirmed pickup or club costs.

steps.text: Track three months of corrections/questions and ask union to protect paid review hours
Apply after cut only for funded school job with written mortgage pay, start and pickup
Keep current paid review rota if no suitable vacancy exists

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Full AGI in 2028 could draft and check the grant accounts I supervise before we have time to price another service. Robots in 2031 come later; they do not rescue a desk role.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the staff committee we need written notice and a real income bridge before posts end. I'd ask the partners to show clients which work still needs a paid accountant rather than promising everybody a new role.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my current post could end in the first year after 2028, even though I am good at it. Our mortgage, two children and less than a month saved make an empty month dangerous. Samir's regular kitchen hours would keep some bills paid but not the house.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I'd stop the planned one-off washing machine upgrade costing six hundred and hold that money for the mortgage, using the old machine while it works. I'd stay employed and inspect only advertised, funded finance jobs with written pay and start dates. If my post ends in the first year after AGI arrives in 2028, I'd claim temporary wage support, then take a suitable role only after its written net pay covers mortgage and any pickup club cost; without one, I'd keep any paid accounts hours and continue applying.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed. The risk is a missing wage in 2028, not a distant change in how accountants work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could Samir increase his hours?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Samir and I would sit down with the mortgage date and the children's timetable that night. He could request more kitchen hours, but we would count only a confirmed paid shift with pickup covered. We cannot spend an offer that has not been made.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the school has no opening?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd take the exact notice letter to the benefits adviser as soon as the firm issues it. A friend at a school cannot give me a post without a funded vacancy, so I'd keep looking. The old machine can be repaired before we buy a new one.

say: I would seek **written notice** and a wage bridge.
I would ask for **paid human work**, not vague reassurance.
think: My **senior desk post** could end in the first year after 2028.
Our **mortgage reserve** lasts less than a month without my accounting wage.
do: Hold the **one-off upgrade money** for mortgage.
After **2028 post loss**, claim support and seek funded work while keeping paid hours.
Accept only **written pay** and a start covering mortgage and pickup costs.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by likely wage loss.
S2.quote: The risk is a missing wage in 2028, not a distant change in how accountants work.
fieldNote: **AGI in 2028** reaches her signed desk work; 2031 robots do not provide extra preparation time.
She **counts confirmed wages only** and keeps paid work while searching if no funded vacancy opens.

steps.text: Delay washing machine upgrade and hold its one-time six hundred for mortgage
Take notice to benefits adviser when issued; claim wage support if post ends after 2028
Take funded finance job after loss only with written net mortgage pay, pickup costs and start
Keep paid accounts hours while searching if no funded post opens

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years lets us find out whether clients will pay for a named person to present complicated grant accounts. AGI in 2031 still reaches most preparation and checking, and the robots around 2034 do not give my desk extra years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the partners for a priced service, not an unpaid reassurance call. I'd tell our union representative that staff need paid time to design it and a clear redeployment rule if the tax desk closes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could lead trustee briefings because clients trust me to explain what a restricted fund means. But the charity's board may choose a cheap automated explanation. Our family cannot rely on a service until a budget holder signs for it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This spring I'd propose a pilot of two trustee briefings on paid work time only if the partner approves the fee and two clients sign a covering booking. I'd keep my current salary while testing it. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2031, if account preparation ends, I'd take a funded school finance opening only with written mortgage-covering net pay, start date and pickup plan; otherwise I'd keep paid briefing work if contracted or claim support and search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, with enough time to test an actual invoice. A polite board thank-you doesn't pay the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would clients actually buy?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: One charity chair asked me to explain why a grant could not pay ordinary heating costs. I enjoyed getting the board to understand it, but the next question is whether they would pay for a full session. I would ask the budget holder, not the chair alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if paid pilot time is refused?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If the partner declines paid pilot time, I won't run free briefings on evenings away from the children. I'd keep my account reviews and take the service proposal to the staff committee. If the signed fees don't cover my hours, the pilot stops rather than becoming a pretend job.

say: I would ask for **priced trustee briefings** that cover staff time.
I would seek **paid pilot time** and redeployment rules through the union.
think: A **board explanation** may remain valuable when automated figures are cheap.
Signed **client budgets** must cover the wages for an actual briefing.
do: Pilot **two trustee briefings** only with partner approval for paid time and budget holders’ signed covering fees, retaining current salary.
After **2031 desk loss**, take funded work only with written wage, start and pickup.
Keep **paid reviews** if pilot refused; after loss retain contracted briefings or seek support while searching if none exists.
feel: I feel **anxious** until paid demand is clear.
S3.quote: A polite board thank-you doesn't pay the mortgage.
fieldNote: The **paid pilot** depends on partner approval and two signed fees covering her hours.
After **2031 desk loss**, school work needs funded vacancy, written net mortgage pay, start and childcare; support covers an unsuccessful search.

steps.text: Pilot two briefings with budget holders’ signed covering fees and approved paid time, retaining current salary
Stop briefings if fees fail or paid time refused; keep reviews and staff discussion
Take funded school finance post after 2031 loss only with written mortgage pay, start and pickup
Keep contracted paid briefings; otherwise seek wage support and posted work after loss without opening

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A decade gives us room to save and test a paid advice service, though AGI in 2036 still takes most account preparation. Robots around 2039 would not change the timing for my desk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask employers and the union for paid transition time and early vacancy notices. I would tell colleagues that a promised future role needs an actual wage line.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 2036 our children will be older, but we still need wages for the mortgage. A trustee briefing service might last if boards renew it, though AGI may explain the figures cheaply too. Right now less than a month saved makes even a long runway feel narrow.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep our monthly budget now and request a written senior pay scale. If it brings a raise, I'd save forty monthly; if not, I won't count a fictional transfer. Over the next two years I'd ask the union for paid transition time and publishable vacancies. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2036, if my desk post ends, I'd take a funded finance role only with written mortgage-covering net pay, a start date and covered pickup; otherwise I'd claim wage support and keep searching while taking any paid briefings available.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the money today, even with ten years to prepare. My children growing up will not make the mortgage disappear.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would older children help with costs?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The older child may have left school by then, but our youngest's plans are their own. We will not put an adult child's hoped-for wage in our home budget. I want an emergency account built from our pay, not theirs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the salary scale stays flat?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If the pay scale stays flat, I can still hold the existing budget and ask about funded openings; I cannot save forty out of thin air. If a trustee briefing contract continues, I will keep that paid work during the search. I will not resign for a role with no written start.

say: I would seek **paid transition time** through the union before work shrinks.
I would demand **vacancy wages** in writing before I decide to move.
think: Our **mortgage** persists when AGI reaches desk work in 2036.
A **long runway** does not create savings from our low pay today.
do: Save **forty monthly** only after a written pay rise.
Ask the **union** for transition time and funded vacancies.
After **2036 post loss**, take funded work with written mortgage pay, start and pickup; otherwise claim support.
feel: I feel **anxious** about thin savings today.
S4.quote: My children growing up will not make the mortgage disappear.
fieldNote: Her **current thin reserve** keeps baseline anxiety present even with a decade before AGI.
The **2036 move** requires funded opening, written mortgage net pay, start and pickup; absent one, she keeps paid work and claims support.

steps.text: Transfer forty monthly only after written senior pay rise
Ask union for paid transition time and published funded vacancies
Take funded finance role after 2036 post loss only with written mortgage pay, start and pickup
Seek support after 2036 loss without vacancy; keep any briefings only while contracted

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI arriving by 2028 worries me most because my accounting wage could end before we have an emergency month. Samir's regular kitchen wage would not cover the mortgage and both children. A written notice period, temporary wage support and funded work with a real start date would let us plan. We cannot spend an offer that has not been made.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask whether a charity will budget for a person to explain the accounts after a machine has prepared them. If the answer is yes, let the staff share that paid work. If it is no, don't call the free board meeting a new career.

headlineQuote: We cannot spend an offer that has not been made.
portrait: At **forty-three**, Beth leads four accountants preparing charity accounts and tax returns.
Her **master’s** and chartered qualification accompany top skill but low senior pay.
She uses **AI occasionally** for tested meeting notes, never unchecked returns.
Samir’s **school wage**, two children, mortgage and less than one month saved leave little slack.
Few **nearby firms** make signed pay, start and pickup conditions essential to a move.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end her accounting wage before the family has one emergency month.
whatWouldHelp: She wants **written notice**, temporary wage support and funded work with a real start.
